Oral antibiotics (such as doxycycline): for moderate acne, usually for no more than 3 to 4 months, alongside a cream. Hormonal treatment: the combined contraceptive pill or spironolactone can help women with hormone-related acne. Isotretinoin tablets: very effective for severe, scarring or persistent acne. In Malaysia, guidelines say it should be prescribed by dermatologists. It causes serious birth defects, so women must use contraception during treatment and for a month afterwards, and doctors monitor blood tests and mood. Be patient: most treatments take 8 to 12 weeks to work. Use them on the whole area, not just on spots, and keep going after the skin clears to prevent relapse. Hydrocolloid acne patches absorb fluid from a spot and, just as importantly, stop you touching and picking it. They can help a single surfaced whitehead heal, but the research is small, and they don’t treat deep cysts or prevent new acne. Don’t pick or squeeze spots. It spreads inflammation and causes scars and dark marks. Don’t scrub , or use toothpaste, lemon or alcohol on spots. Wash twice a day with a gentle cleanser. Don’t use steroid creams on the face. They can worsen acne and cause perioral dermatitis. Avoid unregistered “acne” or “whitening” creams . The National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) has repeatedly cancelled cosmetics found to contain hidden steroids, tretinoin, hydroquinone and mercury, which can thin and damage the skin and harm the kidneys and nerves. Check products on the NPRA website. Dark marks after acne (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation) are very common in Asian skin, affecting up to 87% of acne patients in some studies, and can last more than a year. Treating acne early, sun protection, and azelaic acid or retinoids help them fade. Acne scars affect many people with acne. Once acne is controlled, scars can be improved with treatments such as chemical peels, laser resurfacing and microneedling at a doctor-led aesthetic clinic. See our guide to laser treatments and checking a clinic . Painful, deep nodules or cysts, or acne that is leaving scars or dark marks No improvement after 2 to 3 months of pharmacy treatment Acne affecting your confidence, mood or daily life Sudden adult acne with irregular periods or excess hair, which may be PCOS Itchy bumps on the back and chest that don’t respond to acne treatment Acne during pregnancy, as some treatments aren’t safe Seek help urgently for acne that suddenly becomes painful and ulcerated with fever, or if acne is making you feel hopeless or think about harming yourself. How do I get rid of acne? (Cara hilangkan jerawat) Wash twice daily with a gentle cleanser, don’t pick spots, and use an evidence-based treatment such as benzoyl peroxide, a topical retinoid or azelaic acid for at least 8 to 12 weeks. See a doctor if it doesn’t improve or leaves scars. Why do I get acne on my eyebrows and forehead? (Jerawat di kening) Often from oily skin, oily hair, fringes, and hair or skin products that block pores. Spots caused by hair products can take 4 to 6 weeks to clear after stopping the product. Why do I get spots around my lips? (Jerawat di bibir) Small red bumps around the mouth may be perioral dermatitis rather than acne, often triggered by steroid creams or inhalers. See a doctor, as acne creams can make it worse. Why do I get acne on my bottom? (Jerawat di punggung) Spots on the buttocks are usually folliculitis, inflammation of hair follicles from sweat, friction and tight clothing, rather than acne. Loose cotton clothing and gentle washing help. Do acne patches work? (Patch jerawat) They help single surfaced whiteheads heal and stop you picking, but evidence is limited and they don’t treat deep cysts or prevent new spots. What is fungal acne? Malassezia folliculitis causes small, uniform, itchy bumps on the back and chest, common in hot, humid climates. It is caused by yeast, not acne bacteria, and is treated with antifungals.

title: Bowel cancer in Malaysia: symptoms, free stool test screening and colonoscopy
desc: Bowel cancer is the most common cancer in Malaysian men, and 3 in 4 cases are found late. The symptoms to watch for, who is at risk, the free stool test at government clinics from age 50, and what a colonoscopy involves.
headings: Bowel cancer in Malaysia · Bowel cancer symptoms (kanser usus simptom) · Who is at higher risk? · Free bowel cancer screening: the stool test · If bowel cancer runs in your family · What happens during a colonoscopy · Treatment
keywords: Prevention Bowel cancer screening Colorectal cancer Kanser kolorektal payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Bowel cancer is the most common cancer in Malaysian men and the second most common in women. Cases rose by more than half between 2012–2016 and 2017–2021. About 3 in 4 cases are diagnosed at stage 3 or 4. Early bowel cancer often causes no symptoms. Symptoms include blood in the stool, a change in bowel habit, tummy pain or bloating, unexplained weight loss and tiredness from anaemia. Adults aged 50 to 75 at average risk should do a stool test (iFOBT), free at government health clinics. A positive result needs a colonoscopy. If a close relative had bowel cancer, colonoscopy screening usually starts at 40, or earlier. According to the Malaysia National Cancer Registry report for 2017–2021: Bowel (colorectal) cancer made up 14.1% of all cancers , the second most common overall after breast cancer, and the most common cancer in men . About 23,900 people were diagnosed in those five years, up 54% from 2012–2016. About 15% were under 50. About three in four cases with a known stage were found at stage 3 or 4 . Only about 6% were caught at stage 1. The lifetime risk is about 1 in 44 for men and 1 in 62 for women , and highest among Chinese Malaysians (1 in 30 men). Finding it early makes a big difference. In US data, about 9 in 10 people whose cancer is found before it spreads are alive 5 years later, compared with about 1 in 7 when it has spread to distant organs. Blood in your stool , which may look red or black, or bleeding from the bottom A change in bowel habit , such as looser stools, constipation or going more often, lasting several weeks Feeling you need to go even after you have just been Tummy pain, a lump in the tummy, or bloating Losing weight without trying Tiredness or breathlessness from anaemia (low blood count) Most people with these symptoms don’t have cancer. Haemorrhoids (piles), for example, are a common cause of bleeding. But you can’t tell the difference yourself, so always get bleeding from the bottom checked by a doctor. Malaysian guidelines advise an urgent colonoscopy within 2 weeks for unexplained rectal bleeding with a change in bowel habit or weight loss, or for iron-deficiency anaemia. Early bowel cancer often causes no symptoms at all , which is why screening matters. Being 50 or older , though younger adults can get it A close relative (parent, brother, sister or child) with bowel cancer, or inherited conditions such as Lynch syndrome A history of bowel polyps, or inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis) Smoking, alcohol, being overweight and being inactive A diet high in processed meat (such as sausages, ham and luncheon meat) and red meat, and low in fruit and vegetables. The WHO’s cancer agency classifies processed meat as a cause of bowel cancer. Malaysian guidelines recommend that adults aged 50 to 75 at average risk do an immunochemical faecal occult blood test (iFOBT) , also called a FIT test. It detects tiny amounts of blood in the stool that you can’t see. Where: it is offered free at government health clinics (Klinik Kesihatan) , apart from the registration fee. Ask for it at your next visit. Selangor’s Selangor Saring programme has also included the test. Private clinics and pharmacies offer it for a fee. How: you collect a small stool sample at home with the kit, and return it to the clinic. There are no diet restrictions. How often: the 2017 guidelines recommend yearly testing if negative. Some clinics schedule a repeat every 2 years. If positive: you are referred for a colonoscopy. A positive test doesn’t mean you have cancer. Most positives are due to polyps or other causes, but it must be followed up. Too few Malaysians take part. Between 2014 and 2018, only about 55% of people with a positive stool test went on to have the colonoscopy they needed. In Selangor’s screening programme, only 15–27% of people with abnormal results followed up. If your test is positive, please go for the colonoscopy. The stool test is done at home and returned to the clinic for testing. Malaysian guidelines recommend colonoscopy, rather than the stool test, for people with a family history: Family history When to start colonoscopy A parent, brother, sister or child diagnosed before 60, or any relative before 50 At 40, or 10 years younger than the youngest relative was at diagnosis, whichever is earlier. Repeat every 3 to 5 years. A parent, brother, sister or child diagnosed at 60 or older At 40. Repeat every 10 years. Tell your doctor about your family history, including the age your relative was diagnosed. A colonoscopy uses a thin, flexible tube with a camera to look inside the large bowel. It can find cancer early, and remove polyps before they turn into cancer. Before: you follow a special diet and take a strong laxative to empty the bowel. During: the test usually takes 30 to 45 minutes. You are usually offered sedation and painkillers. Polyps can be removed and small samples (biopsies) taken. After: don’t drive for 24 hours if you had sedation. Slight bleeding for a day or two is common. Risks: serious complications are uncommon. In the UK screening programme, a tear in the bowel happens in about 1 in 1,700 colonoscopies. Surgery to remove the cancer is the main treatment and offers the best chance of cure. Chemotherapy and radiotherapy may be used before or after surgery, and newer targeted treatments and immunotherapy help some people with advanced cancer. Treatment is planned by a team of specialists. You can lower your risk by staying active, keeping a healthy weight, not smoking, limiting alcohol, eating less processed and red meat, and eating more fruit and vegetables. What are the symptoms of bowel cancer? (Kanser usus simptom) Blood in the stool or bleeding from the bottom, a change in bowel habit lasting weeks, tummy pain or bloating, unexplained weight loss, and tiredness from anaemia. Early bowel cancer often has no symptoms. Is bowel cancer screening free in Malaysia? Yes. The iFOBT stool test is offered free at government health clinics for adults aged 50 to 75 at average risk, apart from the registration fee. A positive result is followed by a colonoscopy at a government hospital. How is the iFOBT stool test done? You collect a small stool sample at home using the kit and return it to the clinic. It detects hidden blood. There are no diet restrictions. At what age should I start bowel cancer screening? At 50 for most people. If a close relative had bowel cancer, colonoscopy usually starts at 40, or 10 years before the age your relative was diagnosed, if they were under 60. Can bowel cancer affect young people? Yes. About 15% of bowel cancers in Malaysia in 2017–2021 were in people under 50. Don’t ignore symptoms such as bleeding because you are young. Is bleeding from the bottom always cancer? No. Haemorrhoids (piles) and fissures are common causes. But you can’t tell the cause yourself, so always have rectal bleeding checked by a doctor.

title: High blood pressure and cholesterol: signs, normal levels, and how to lower them
desc: Nearly 1 in 3 Malaysian adults has high blood pressure, and 1 in 3 has high cholesterol, often without knowing. Normal levels, causes, what really lowers them and how fast, and what to know about blood pressure and cholesterol medicines.
headings: How common are they in Malaysia? · Blood pressure levels · Signs of high blood pressure (tanda darah tinggi) · What causes high blood pressure? (Punca darah tinggi) · How to lower blood pressure · Blood pressure medicines · Normal cholesterol levels (kadar kolesterol normal) · How to lower cholesterol · Side effects of cholesterol medicine (kesan sampingan ubat kolesterol)
keywords: Heart & diabetes Blood pressure and cholesterol Hypertension Darah tinggi kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah kecemasan emergency a&e hospital
body: 29.2% of Malaysian adults have high blood pressure and 33.3% have high cholesterol, according to NHMS 2023. Many don’t know. High blood pressure usually has no signs. Only a blood pressure check can tell you. A reading of 140/90 or above, on repeated checks, is high. There is no safe way to lower blood pressure in 5 minutes. Very high blood pressure with chest pain, breathlessness, weakness or vision changes is an emergency: call 999. Cutting salt to less than 1 teaspoon a day, losing weight, exercise and less alcohol can lower blood pressure by several points each. Statins lower LDL cholesterol by about 20–55%. True statin side effects are less common than many people think. According to the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2023: 29.2% of adults have high blood pressure, and 11.9% of adults, about 2.7 million people, have it without knowing. Of those who are treated, fewer than half have it under control. 33.3% have high cholesterol, and about half of them don’t know. More than 60% of adults aged 18 to 39 with diabetes, high blood pressure or high cholesterol were unaware of it. Ischaemic heart disease, which both conditions lead to, is Malaysia’s leading cause of death. See our article on undiagnosed conditions in young adults . Blood pressure is written as two numbers: the top (systolic) is the pressure when the heart beats, and the bottom (diastolic) is the pressure between beats. Malaysia’s hypertension guidelines classify it as: Reading (mmHg) Category Below 120/80 Optimal 120–129 / 80–84 Normal 130–139 / 85–89 At risk 140–159 / 90–99 Stage 1 (mild) hypertension 160–179 / 100–109 Stage 2 (moderate) 180 / 110 or higher Stage 3 (severe) One high reading doesn’t mean you have hypertension. Doctors confirm it with repeated readings, often at home. See our guide to checking your blood pressure at home . On treatment, the target for most people is below 140/90, and lower for some people with diabetes, kidney disease or heart disease. High blood pressure is called a “silent disease” . Most people feel completely well. Headaches, dizziness or tiredness are not reliable signs, and only a blood pressure check can tell you. When high blood pressure is an emergency A reading of 180/110 or higher needs prompt medical attention. Call 999 or go to an emergency department straight away if it comes with chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, confusion, weakness or numbness, difficulty speaking, or vision changes. If you have no symptoms, sit quietly for 5 minutes, recheck, and see a doctor the same day if it is still very high. Most high blood pressure has no single cause. It builds up with: Too much salt . Malaysians eat around 8 to 9.5 g of salt a day, well above the recommended limit Being overweight, and not being active Alcohol and smoking Getting older, and having a family history Stress Sometimes another condition or medicine is the cause, especially in younger people. Examples include kidney disease, sleep apnoea (heavy snoring with daytime sleepiness), thyroid or hormone problems, and medicines such as anti-inflammatory painkillers, steroids, decongestants and the contraceptive pill. Tell your doctor about any traditional or herbal remedies you take, too. Can you lower blood pressure in 5 minutes? No, not safely. Slow, deep breathing may bring it down a little for a short time, and practised regularly it can help a few points. But there is no quick fix, and Malaysian guidelines warn that lowering very high blood pressure too fast can itself cause a stroke or heart attack. If a reading is very high, follow the emergency advice above. What does work, over weeks to months, according to Malaysia’s hypertension guidelines: Change Typical effect on blood pressure Cut salt to less than 5 g (about 1 teaspoon) a day Up to about 8/3 mmHg lower in Asian adults with hypertension Lose weight About 1 mmHg lower per kg lost A healthy diet rich in fruit, vegetables and low-fat dairy Several points lower 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week Several points lower Cut down alcohol About 3/2 mmHg lower Cooking with less salt, soy sauce and stock cubes, and choosing fewer processed and hawker foods, makes the biggest difference for most Malaysians. If lifestyle changes aren’t enough, or your blood pressure is high, your doctor will prescribe one or more medicines. The main groups are ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), calcium channel blockers, diuretics and beta blockers. Common side effects to know: ACE inhibitors (names often end in “-pril”): a dry, persistent cough in some people. Your doctor can switch you to an ARB. Calcium channel blockers such as amlodipine: ankle swelling, flushing or headache. Beta blockers : tiredness and cold hands and feet. Most people need treatment for life. Don’t stop your medicine when your readings become normal, because that usually means the medicine is working. Talk to your doctor about any side effects instead. A cholesterol test measures several fats in the blood. You usually don’t need to fast. Malaysian guidelines use these levels to flag a problem: Test Flag level (mmol/L) Total cholesterol Above 5.2 is high LDL (“bad”) cholesterol Target depends on your heart risk (see below) HDL (“good”) cholesterol Below 1.0 in men or 1.2 in women is low Triglycerides Above 1.7 is high LDL targets depend on your risk. The higher your risk of a heart attack or stroke, the lower your LDL should be. For people at very high risk, such as after a heart attack or stroke, Malaysia’s 2023 guidelines aim for 1.4 mmol/L or lower and a reduction of more than half. Your doctor will work out your risk using your age, blood pressure, smoking, diabetes and family history. Cut down on saturated fat (fatty meat, coconut milk and ghee-heavy dishes, butter) and avoid trans fats in fried snacks and baked goods. Eat more fibre: oats, whole grains, beans, fruit and vegetables. About 3 g of oat beta-glucan a day lowers LDL slightly. Choose fewer refined carbohydrates, such as large servings of white rice and sweet drinks. Exercise regularly, lose weight if you are overweight, and stop smoking. How fast? Diet changes take weeks to months. Statins usually reach their full effect within about a month, and doctors recheck cholesterol 1 to 3 months after starting. Statins are the main cholesterol medicine. They lower LDL by about 20 to 55%, depending on the type and dose, and reduce heart attacks and strokes. Other medicines, such as ezetimibe, can be added. Statins are among the most studied medicines in the world, and serious side effects are rare: Muscle aches: many people report them, but in trials they happen only slightly more often than with a dummy pill. In one study, people who had stopped statins because of side effects felt almost the same symptoms when taking a placebo. Serious muscle damage is rare. Most people who can’t tolerate one statin do fine on another. Liver: a mild rise in liver tests happens in under 3% of people. Liver failure is extremely rare. Diabetes: statins slightly increase the chance of developing diabetes, mainly in people already at risk, but the heart benefits are far greater. Don’t stop a statin on your own. If you have side effects, talk to your doctor about changing the dose or type. More vegetables, fruit, oats and beans, and less saturated fat, help lower cholesterol. What are the signs of high blood pressure? (Tanda darah tinggi) Usually none. High blood pressure is a “silent disease”, and only a blood pressure check can tell you. Very high blood pressure with chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, weakness or vision changes is an emergency. How can I lower my blood pressure quickly? (Cara menurunkan darah tinggi dengan cepat) There is no safe way to lower it within minutes, and lowering very high blood pressure too fast can be dangerous. Over weeks, cutting salt, losing weight, exercise and less alcohol all help. If a reading is 180/110 or higher with symptoms, call 999. What is a normal cholesterol level? (Kadar kolesterol normal) Malaysian guidelines flag total cholesterol above 5.2 mmol/L, HDL below 1.0 (men) or 1.2 (women), and triglycerides above 1.7. Your LDL target depends on your heart risk. What are the side effects of cholesterol medicine? (Kesan ubat kolesterol) Statins can cause muscle aches in some people, mild liver test changes and a slightly higher diabetes risk, but serious side effects are rare. Talk to your doctor rather than stopping it yourself. Can I stop my blood pressure medicine when my readings are normal? No. Normal readings usually mean the medicine is working. Most people need it long term. Talk to your doctor before changing anything. How fast can I lower my cholesterol? (Menurunkan kolesterol dengan cepat) Statins reach their full effect in about a month. Diet changes take weeks to months. Your doctor will usually recheck cholesterol 1 to 3 months after a change.

title: Vertigo and dizziness: common causes, exercises that help, and when it’s a stroke
desc: A brief spin when you roll over in bed is usually BPPV, which a simple head manoeuvre often fixes. The common causes of vertigo and dizziness, exercises that help, what anti-dizziness medicines can and can’t do, and the signs that dizziness is a stroke.
headings: Vertigo or dizziness? · Why does vertigo happen? (Sebab vertigo) · Exercises for vertigo at home · Medicines for vertigo, including cinnarizine · When dizziness is a stroke · Staying safe, and when to see a doctor
keywords: Guides Vertigo and dizziness Vertigo Vertigo (pening berpusing) kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital
body: Vertigo is a spinning sensation. Dizziness can also mean feeling light-headed, faint or unsteady, which often has different causes. The most common cause is BPPV: brief spinning, usually under a minute, when you roll over in bed, look up or bend down. The Epley manoeuvre fixes BPPV in about 7 or 8 in 10 people after one to three treatments. Anti-dizziness tablets aren’t recommended for BPPV. Medicines such as cinnarizine and betahistine are available from pharmacists in Malaysia, but should only be used for a few days, as they can slow recovery and cause drowsiness. Call 999 for vertigo with double vision, slurred speech, weakness, numbness, sudden hearing loss or inability to walk. It may be a stroke. Vertigo: a false sense that you or your surroundings are spinning or moving. It usually comes from the inner ear, and sometimes from the brain. Light-headedness: feeling faint or about to pass out, often from low blood pressure, dehydration, low blood sugar or anaemia. Imbalance: feeling unsteady on your feet, common in older people. Telling your doctor what it feels like, how long it lasts, and what brings it on is the most useful information for working out the cause. About 1 in 13 people have vertigo from an inner ear or balance problem at some point in their lives, more often women and older adults. Cause Typical pattern BPPV (benign paroxysmal positional vertigo) Brief spinning, usually under 1 minute, triggered by rolling over in bed, looking up or bending down. Caused by tiny crystals in the inner ear moving out of place. Hearing is normal. Most common in people in their 50s to 70s, and after head injury. Vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis Sudden, severe vertigo lasting days, often after a cold or flu, with nausea and vomiting. Labyrinthitis also affects hearing or causes ringing. Balance usually recovers over 2 to 6 weeks. Ménière’s disease Attacks of vertigo, usually lasting 20 minutes to several hours, with hearing loss, ringing (tinnitus) and a feeling of pressure in one ear Vestibular migraine Vertigo lasting minutes to days, often with migraine headaches or sensitivity to light. More common in women. Low blood pressure on standing Light-headedness when getting up quickly, from dehydration, some blood pressure medicines, diabetes or older age Other causes Low blood sugar in diabetes, anaemia, anxiety, heat exhaustion, and new medicines In older adults, medicines are a common cause of dizziness. Bring a list of your medicines to your doctor. The Epley manoeuvre is a series of head and body positions that move the loose crystals back to where they belong. It is the recommended treatment for the most common type of BPPV: About 7 or 8 in 10 people improve after one to three treatments. It works far better than older home exercises (Brandt-Daroff exercises). You don’t need to sleep upright or restrict head movements afterwards. The manoeuvre depends on which ear is affected, so it is best to have a doctor or physiotherapist confirm the diagnosis and do it the first time. They can then teach you how to repeat it at home if the vertigo comes back. Vestibular rehabilitation is a programme of balance and eye-head exercises, guided by a physiotherapist. It helps the brain adapt after vestibular neuritis, and for lasting unsteadiness. Keeping gently active and walking early, rather than staying in bed, also speeds recovery. Balance exercises, guided by a physiotherapist, help the brain adapt after an inner ear problem. Anti-dizziness medicines, called vestibular suppressants, can ease severe symptoms for a short time: Cinnarizine , dimenhydrinate and promethazine (antihistamines) and betahistine can be supplied by a pharmacist in Malaysia without a prescription. Prochlorperazine , for severe nausea and vertigo, needs a prescription. Use them only for a few days. In vestibular neuritis, taking them for longer than about 3 days can slow the brain’s natural recovery. They aren’t recommended for BPPV. They don’t fix the cause, and they increase the risk of falls. Side effects: cinnarizine commonly causes drowsiness, so don’t drive or drink alcohol. Rarely, especially in older people with long-term use, it can cause stiff, slow or jerky movements. Betahistine, used mainly for Ménière’s disease, usually doesn’t cause drowsiness. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before using these medicines if you are older, pregnant, or have Parkinson’s disease, glaucoma, or liver or kidney disease. A stroke in the back of the brain can cause sudden vertigo, and sometimes looks just like an inner ear infection. In one study, vertigo was the first symptom in nearly half of people with this type of stroke. A normal CT scan doesn’t rule it out. Call 999 if vertigo or dizziness comes with Double vision or loss of vision Slurred speech or difficulty speaking Weakness, numbness or tingling in the face, arm or leg Clumsiness, or being unable to stand or walk Sudden hearing loss in one ear Remember BE FAST : Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech, Time to call 999. The risk is higher in people over 50, and those with high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, an irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation), a previous mini-stroke, or who smoke. See our stroke and heart attack guide . Sit or lie down as soon as you feel dizzy. Lying still in a quiet, dark room helps during an attack. Get up slowly, sitting on the edge of the bed for a minute first. Don’t drive, climb ladders or use machinery while dizzy. Older people should take extra care to prevent falls. About 1 in 3 adults over 65 falls each year. See a doctor if vertigo keeps coming back or doesn’t settle, if you aren’t improving after a few days of an inner ear infection, or if dizziness started after a new medicine. Get urgent help for vertigo with a severe headache, vomiting that won’t stop, fever, or sudden hearing loss. What causes vertigo? (Sebab vertigo) The most common cause is BPPV, when tiny crystals in the inner ear move out of place. Others include inner ear infections (vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis), Ménière’s disease and vestibular migraine. Rarely, it is a stroke. What exercise can I do for vertigo at home? For BPPV, the Epley manoeuvre is the most effective treatment. Have a doctor or physiotherapist confirm which ear is affected and do it the first time, then they can teach you to repeat it at home. Is cinnarizine good for vertigo? Cinnarizine can ease severe vertigo and nausea for a few days, and a pharmacist can supply it in Malaysia. It causes drowsiness, isn’t recommended for BPPV, and long-term use can slow recovery and, rarely, cause movement problems in older people. How long does vertigo last? BPPV attacks last under a minute but can recur for weeks until treated. Vestibular neuritis causes severe vertigo for a few days, with balance recovering over 2 to 6 weeks. Ménière’s attacks last 20 minutes to several hours. How do I know if dizziness is a stroke? Call 999 if dizziness comes with double vision, slurred speech, weakness or numbness, clumsiness, being unable to walk, or sudden hearing loss. Use BE FAST: Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech, Time. Why do I feel dizzy when I stand up? Usually because blood pressure drops briefly when you stand, especially if you are dehydrated, older, diabetic or on blood pressure medicines. Get up slowly, drink enough fluids, and see a doctor if it keeps happening.

title: Pregnancy due date calculator and week-by-week guide for Malaysia
desc: Find your due date and how many weeks pregnant you are, then see what happens at each stage of pregnancy in Malaysia: antenatal check-ups, tests, vaccines and the warning signs to know.
headings: Due date calculator · How your due date is worked out · Pregnancy week by week in Malaysia · Antenatal care in Malaysia · Folic acid, iron and vaccines · Early signs of pregnancy and when to test · Ectopic pregnancy (hamil luar rahim) · Warning signs later in pregnancy · Pregnancy in Malaysia: the numbers
keywords: Women's health Pregnancy due date calculator Pregnancy Kehamilan denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Your due date is usually worked out as 40 weeks (280 days) from the first day of your last period. An early pregnancy scan gives a more accurate date. A pregnancy is full term from 39 weeks. Babies born between 37 and 42 weeks are not considered premature or overdue. Book your first antenatal check-up at a Klinik Kesihatan as soon as you can, ideally before 12 weeks, and bring your pink antenatal book to every visit. Take folic acid (400 mcg a day) from before pregnancy until at least 12 weeks. The whooping cough (Tdap) jab is free at government clinics at 28 to 32 weeks. One-sided tummy pain with bleeding or dizziness in early pregnancy can mean an ectopic pregnancy. Get urgent help. Enter the first day of your last period and your usual cycle length. The calculator shows your estimated due date, how many weeks pregnant you are, and when key check-ups fall. First day of your last period Usual cycle length 21 days 22 days 23 days 24 days 25 days 26 days 27 days 28 days 29 days 30 days 31 days 32 days 33 days 34 days 35 days 36 days 37 days 38 days 39 days 40 days 41 days 42 days 43 days 44 days 45 days Calculate Worked out in your browser: nothing you enter is stored or sent. An early pregnancy scan gives the most accurate due date. This calculator needs JavaScript. To work out your due date yourself, add 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of your last period. From your last period: the standard method counts 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of your last menstrual period. This assumes a 28-day cycle, with ovulation around day 14. If your cycles are usually longer or shorter, the calculator shifts the date by the difference. From an early scan: an ultrasound in the first trimester, which measures the baby, is more accurate. If it differs from the date based on your period by more than about a week, doctors usually go by the scan. The Ministry of Health’s perinatal manual says scan dates should be set before 22 weeks. After IVF: the due date is set from the embryo transfer date: 261 days after a 5-day embryo transfer, or 263 days after a 3-day transfer. A due date is an estimate. Pregnancy normally lasts between 37 and 42 weeks, and few babies arrive on the exact day. Weeks of pregnancy What it’s called Before 37 weeks Preterm (premature) 37 weeks to 38 weeks 6 days Early term 39 weeks to 40 weeks 6 days Full term 41 weeks to 41 weeks 6 days Late term 42 weeks or more Post-term If your periods are irregular, you stopped the contraceptive pill recently, or you aren’t sure of the date, your doctor will arrange a dating scan. Stage What usually happens First trimester up to 12 weeks Early signs such as a missed period, nausea and tiredness. Book your first antenatal check-up before 12 weeks. Booking blood and urine tests, and a dating scan if needed. Folic acid and iron. Second trimester 13 to 27 weeks Nausea often eases. Check-ups at around 16–20 and 24–26 weeks. A mid-pregnancy scan. A glucose tolerance test at 24–26 weeks if you are at risk of diabetes in pregnancy. You may start to feel the baby move. Third trimester 28 weeks onwards More frequent check-ups. Start counting your baby’s kicks from 28 weeks. The free whooping cough (Tdap) vaccine at 28–32 weeks. Plan where you will give birth. 37 to 42 weeks Your baby can arrive any time. Weekly check-ups in a first pregnancy. Know the signs of labour, and when to go to hospital. Regular antenatal check-ups pick up problems such as high blood pressure and diabetes in pregnancy early. When and where: register at your nearest Klinik Kesihatan, or with a private doctor, as soon as possible, preferably before 12 weeks . Government clinics give you a pink antenatal record book (Buku Rekod Kesihatan Ibu). Bring it to every appointment, including private ones and when you go into labour. How many check-ups: under the Ministry of Health’s Perinatal Care Manual, a healthy first pregnancy has around 10 visits: before 12 weeks, at 16–20, 24–26, 28–30, 32–34 and 35–36 weeks, then weekly from 37 to 40 weeks. Later pregnancies have around 8. You will have more if you have a higher-risk pregnancy. Colour codes in the pink book: government clinics tag each pregnancy by risk. White means no risk factors, green is followed up by a clinic doctor, yellow needs a specialist, and red needs immediate referral to hospital. Tests at your first visit usually include: Blood pressure, weight and a urine test for protein and sugar Haemoglobin, blood group and Rhesus type Screening for syphilis and HIV, and for hepatitis B where indicated Thalassaemia screening if your red blood cells are small. If you are a carrier, your husband is tested too. See our thalassaemia guide . Diabetes in pregnancy: you’ll be offered a glucose tolerance test if you have risk factors, such as a BMI over 27, diabetes in a close relative, a previous baby weighing 4 kg or more, or diabetes in a previous pregnancy. Folic acid: 400 micrograms a day, ideally from 3 months before you conceive until at least 12 weeks of pregnancy, to lower the risk of spina bifida. Women with diabetes or a previous baby with a neural tube defect need a higher 5 mg dose from their doctor. Iron: anaemia is common in pregnancy in Malaysia, and antenatal clinics routinely give iron supplements. Whooping cough (Tdap): free at Ministry of Health clinics since May 2025, given at 28 to 32 weeks . It passes protection to your baby, who is too young to be vaccinated in the first weeks of life. Flu vaccine: recommended in pregnancy by the Ministry of Health. See our flu vaccine guide . Common early signs, usually from 4 to 6 weeks, include a missed period, light spotting, nausea or vomiting, tiredness, sore breasts, needing to pass urine more often, and a metallic taste. Home pregnancy tests are most reliable from the first day of a missed period . If you don’t know when your period is due, test at least 21 days after unprotected sex. A positive result is almost certainly correct. A negative result is less reliable, so test again a few days later if your period still hasn’t come. In an ectopic pregnancy, the fertilised egg implants outside the womb, usually in a fallopian tube. It affects about 1 in 90 pregnancies and can’t continue safely. Symptoms usually appear between 4 and 12 weeks: Pain low down in the tummy, often on one side Vaginal bleeding or a brown, watery discharge Pain in the tip of the shoulder Discomfort when passing urine or opening your bowels Risk factors include a previous ectopic pregnancy, pelvic infection, tubal surgery, IVF, becoming pregnant with a coil (IUD) in place, smoking and being over 35. Call 999 or go to an emergency department Sudden, severe tummy pain with dizziness, fainting, feeling sick or looking very pale in early pregnancy can mean an ectopic pregnancy has ruptured. This is an emergency. Contact your clinic or go to hospital straight away if you have Bleeding from the vagina, or fluid leaking A severe headache, blurred vision or flashing lights Sudden swelling of the face, hands or feet Severe tummy pain, or regular tightenings before 37 weeks A fever of 38°C or more, or severe vomiting Your baby moving less than usual, or fewer than 10 movements in 12 hours from 28 weeks A fit, or sudden breathlessness A fever in pregnancy can also be dengue, which needs prompt assessment. See our guide to dengue warning signs . Malaysia recorded 396,175 live births in 2025 , 4.5% fewer than in 2024, and the fertility rate fell to a record low of 1.5 children per woman, according to the Department of Statistics. Maternal deaths fell to 20.4 per 100,000 live births in 2025, from 24.3 in 2024. Under the Employment Act, working mothers are entitled to 98 days of maternity leave , and married fathers to 7 days of paid paternity leave , subject to conditions. How do I calculate how many weeks pregnant I am? (Kiraan minggu hamil) Count the weeks from the first day of your last period. You are counted as pregnant from that date, about two weeks before conception. The calculator above does this for you and adjusts for your cycle length. How accurate is a due date calculator? It gives an estimate. Pregnancy normally lasts 37 to 42 weeks, and few babies arrive on the exact day. An ultrasound scan in early pregnancy gives a more accurate due date, and your doctor will use it if it differs from your period date. When should I go for my first antenatal check-up in Malaysia? As soon as possible, preferably before 12 weeks. Register at your nearest Klinik Kesihatan or see a private doctor, and keep your pink antenatal book with you. What are the signs of an ectopic pregnancy (hamil luar rahim)? Pain low in the tummy, often on one side, vaginal bleeding or brown discharge, shoulder-tip pain, and discomfort when passing urine or opening your bowels, usually between 4 and 12 weeks. Sudden severe pain with dizziness or fainting is an emergency. When can I take a pregnancy test? Most home tests are reliable from the first day of a missed period. If you aren’t sure when your period is due, test at least 21 days after unprotected sex. Is the Tdap vaccine free for pregnant women in Malaysia? Yes. Since May 2025, Ministry of Health clinics offer the whooping cough (Tdap) vaccine free to pregnant women at 28 to 32 weeks.

title: Baby and child vaccination schedule in Malaysia: what each jab is for, and what to expect
desc: Malaysia’s free childhood vaccines, age by age: what your baby gets at birth, 2, 3 and 5 months, what the 6-in-1 jab covers, normal side effects, when to call a doctor, and optional extras.
headings: The National Immunisation Programme schedule · What is the 6-in-1 vaccine? · Why keeping to the schedule matters · What to expect after the jabs · Where to get vaccines, and what they cost · Vaccines in pregnancy protect your baby too
keywords: Prevention Baby vaccination schedule Vaccination Imunisasi mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp
body: National Immunisation Programme vaccines are free for Malaysian children at government health clinics (Klinik Kesihatan). At 2, 3 and 5 months, babies get the 6-in-1 vaccine, which protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib and hepatitis B, with a booster at 18 months. Pneumococcal vaccine is given at 4 and 6 months with a booster at 15 months, and MMR at 9 and 12 months. Fever, fussiness and a sore leg for a day or two are common. Seek urgent help for a fit, a very high fever, or signs of an allergic reaction. Measles cases nearly doubled to 3,791 in 2024, and young babies died of whooping cough in 2023. Keep to the schedule, and catch up on missed doses. This is the Ministry of Health schedule, as published on the government’s MyGOV portal in 2026: Age Vaccine Protects against Birth BCG; hepatitis B (within 24 hours) Tuberculosis; hepatitis B 2 months 6-in-1 (dose 1) Diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib, hepatitis B 3 months 6-in-1 (dose 2) As above 4 months Pneumococcal (dose 1) Pneumonia, meningitis and blood infections caused by pneumococcus 5 months 6-in-1 (dose 3) As above 6 months Pneumococcal (dose 2); measles (Sabah only) Pneumococcus; measles 9 months MMR (dose 1); Japanese encephalitis (Sarawak only) Measles, mumps, rubella; Japanese encephalitis 12 months MMR (dose 2) Measles, mumps, rubella 15 months Pneumococcal booster Pneumococcus 18 months 6-in-1 booster Diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib, hepatitis B 21 months Japanese encephalitis booster (Sarawak only) Japanese encephalitis 7 years DT booster Diphtheria, tetanus Year 6 (girls) HPV (single dose) The virus behind most cervical cancers 15 years Tetanus booster Tetanus Your child’s clinic may adjust timing, for example for premature babies. Babies still have growth and development checks at 1 and 6 months, even where no vaccine is due. Since November 2020, Malaysia has used a hexavalent (6-in-1) vaccine , which combines protection against six diseases in one injection: diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (whooping cough), polio, Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) and hepatitis B. It replaced an older 5-in-1 vaccine plus separate hepatitis B shots, cutting the number of injections a baby needs. Parents often search for it by brand name, such as “Hexaxim”, which is one brand of 6-in-1 vaccine. The government programme and private clinics may use different brands. They protect against the same six diseases. Babies have their first 6-in-1 vaccine at 2 months, then at 3 and 5 months, with a booster at 18 months. Vaccine-preventable diseases are returning where coverage slips: Measles cases rose from 2,002 in 2023 to 3,791 in 2024 , and 44% of cases were in children under 5. Although national coverage is high, only 62% of districts reached the 95% MMR coverage needed to stop outbreaks. Whooping cough killed 43 babies under 5 months old in 2023 , babies too young to be fully vaccinated. That is why the vaccine is now offered free in pregnancy too. Recorded vaccine refusals rose from 637 in 2013 to 1,603 in 2016. Vaccines give the best protection when given on time. If your child has missed a dose, talk to your clinic about catching up. In most cases a delayed dose is simply given, and the course doesn’t need to start again. Most reactions are mild and settle within 2 to 3 days: Redness, swelling, soreness or a small lump where the injection was given A mild fever Fussiness, sleepiness or a poor appetite for a day or so Offer extra feeds and cuddles, and dress your baby lightly. If your baby has a fever and seems uncomfortable, ask the clinic or a pharmacist about paracetamol , dosed by weight. Never give aspirin to children. Get urgent medical help if your child Has a fit (seizure) Has a temperature of 39°C or higher, or seems very unwell Cries non-stop for 3 hours or more Has signs of an allergic reaction: swelling of the face or lips, difficulty breathing, or a widespread rash. Call 999. A fit caused by fever (a febrile seizure) is frightening, but usually stops on its own and doesn’t cause lasting harm. Always get your child checked afterwards. Government health clinics (Klinik Kesihatan): all National Immunisation Programme vaccines are free for Malaysian children. Non-citizens pay a fee. Private clinics: can give the same vaccines for a fee, and often offer optional extras. Records: keep your child’s health record book safe, as it is needed for primary school registration. For babies born from July 2022, vaccination records also appear in MySejahtera. Optional vaccines commonly offered privately, which are not part of the free programme, include rotavirus, chickenpox (varicella), influenza, hepatitis A, meningococcal and typhoid vaccines, and pneumococcal vaccines covering more strains. Ask your doctor which are worth considering for your child. Flu vaccines for children are covered in our flu vaccine guide . Since May 2025, Ministry of Health clinics offer the whooping cough (Tdap) vaccine free to pregnant women at 28 to 32 weeks . Antibodies pass to the baby and protect them in the first weeks of life, before their own 6-in-1 doses start. The flu vaccine is also recommended in pregnancy. See our pregnancy guide and due date calculator . Which vaccines does a baby get at 2 months in Malaysia? (Vaksin bayi 2 bulan) The first dose of the 6-in-1 vaccine, which protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib and hepatitis B. Further doses follow at 3 and 5 months, with a booster at 18 months. What is Hexaxim for? (Hexaxim vaksin apa) Hexaxim is one brand of 6-in-1 (hexavalent) vaccine. It protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib and hepatitis B. The government programme gives a 6-in-1 vaccine free at 2, 3, 5 and 18 months. Are baby vaccines free in Malaysia? Yes. National Immunisation Programme vaccines are free for Malaysian children at government health clinics. Private clinics charge for the same vaccines and for optional ones. Is fever normal after a baby’s vaccination? A mild fever and fussiness for a day or two is common. Seek urgent help for a fit, a temperature of 39°C or more, non-stop crying for 3 hours or more, or signs of an allergic reaction. What if my child missed a vaccine? Talk to your clinic about catching up. In most cases the missed dose is simply given late, and the course doesn’t need to restart. Is the rotavirus vaccine free in Malaysia? No. Rotavirus, chickenpox, influenza and some other vaccines aren’t part of the free national programme, but are available at private clinics.

title: Gout in Malaysia: symptoms, uric acid levels, foods to limit and treatment
desc: Gout causes sudden, severe joint pain, often in the big toe at night. What your uric acid level means, which foods and drinks trigger attacks, why painkillers alone aren’t enough, and how gout differs from pseudogout.
headings: What is gout? · Gout symptoms: what an attack feels like · What your uric acid level means · What causes gout, and foods to limit · Treating gout · Gout or pseudogout? · Why gout needs long-term care
keywords: Heart & diabetes Gout Gout Gout (asid urik) kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Gout is caused by uric acid crystals in a joint. Attacks usually start suddenly, often at night, with severe pain, redness and swelling, most often in the big toe. A uric acid level above 408 µmol/L (6.8 mg/dL) is high, but a high level alone doesn’t mean gout, and the level can be normal during an attack. Alcohol, sugary drinks, red meat, some seafood and excess weight raise the risk. Some blood pressure medicines can too. Attacks are treated with colchicine, anti-inflammatories or steroids. People with repeated attacks need long-term uric acid-lowering medicine, aiming for below 360 µmol/L. Don’t stop uric acid-lowering medicine during an attack, and never try to drain gout lumps (tophi) yourself. Gout happens when uric acid , a waste product the body makes when it breaks down substances called purines, builds up in the blood and forms needle-like crystals in a joint. The immune system attacks the crystals, causing sudden, intense inflammation. There are no national figures on how common gout is in Malaysia. Hospital studies show it usually starts between the ages of 30 and 60 and mostly affects men. Specialists say they are seeing more young adults with gout, linked to rising obesity, and nearly half of Malaysians are overweight. Sudden, severe pain in one joint, often starting at night and peaking within 24 hours. Many people describe it as throbbing, burning or like being stabbed. The joint becomes red, hot and swollen , and too painful to touch, even with a bedsheet. The big toe is the most common site, followed by the midfoot and ankle. Knees, wrists, hands and elbows can also be affected. Some people have a fever during an attack. Attacks usually settle within a week or two, but without treatment they tend to come back more often and affect more joints. Over time, firm white or yellow lumps called tophi can form under the skin, at the toes, ears, elbows and fingers. Don’t drain gout lumps yourself Puncturing a tophus at home can cause a serious, even life-threatening, infection. See a doctor if a lump is painful, open or leaking. Also see a doctor urgently for a hot, swollen joint with a high fever, as it could be a joint infection. Uric acid level What it means Above 408 µmol/L (6.8 mg/dL) High (hyperuricaemia): crystals can start to form Below 360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL) Treatment target for people on uric acid-lowering medicine Below 300 µmol/L (5 mg/dL) Target for severe gout, such as with tophi or frequent attacks Reference ranges vary slightly between laboratories, so check the range printed on your report. A high level isn’t the same as gout. Many people with high uric acid never get an attack, and Malaysian guidelines don’t recommend treating high uric acid without symptoms. The level can be normal during an attack. Doctors may repeat the test two or more weeks after the attack settles. Things that raise the risk of gout, according to the Ministry of Health’s gout guidelines: Being overweight Alcohol, including beer Sugar-sweetened drinks and fruit juice Red meat, organ meats and some seafood, such as anchovies, sardines and shellfish Some medicines, including diuretics (“water pills”) and some blood pressure medicines Kidney disease, diabetes, a family history of gout, and being male or past menopause Foods that may help: dairy products are linked to a lower risk, and purines from plant foods such as beans and vegetables don’t raise it. Cherries may lower the chance of attacks, but the evidence is limited. Losing weight, drinking enough water and cutting alcohol and sweet drinks all help. Don’t stop any prescribed medicine, including low-dose aspirin for your heart, without talking to your doctor. They can switch blood pressure medicines if needed. During an attack: your doctor may prescribe colchicine, an anti-inflammatory painkiller (NSAID), or a steroid. Rest the joint, raise it, and apply an ice pack wrapped in a towel for up to 20 minutes. Start treatment as early as you can. Preventing attacks: painkillers treat the pain, but not the cause. People with repeated attacks, tophi or kidney stones usually need long-term uric acid-lowering medicine , most often allopurinol, to bring the level below the target. It is started at a low dose and increased slowly, with regular blood tests. Doctors often add a low-dose anti-inflammatory for the first 3 to 6 months, as attacks can briefly increase when treatment starts. Keep taking it during an attack , and long term. Stopping is the most common reason treatment fails. In one Malaysian clinic, only about a third of patients reached their target. Rarely, allopurinol causes a serious skin reaction. Stop it and see a doctor at once if you get a rash, blisters or mouth sores. Long-term uric acid-lowering treatment needs regular check-ups and blood tests. Pseudogout (calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease) causes similar sudden, painful, swollen joints, but it is caused by calcium crystals , not uric acid. It is more common in people over 60, most often affects the knee , and attacks last 1 to 2 weeks. It doesn’t respond to uric acid-lowering medicine. A doctor can tell them apart by testing fluid from the joint, or from X-ray findings. Untreated gout can lead to permanent joint damage, tophi, kidney stones and kidney disease. People with gout also have higher rates of heart disease, diabetes and high blood pressure, so a check of your blood pressure , blood sugar, cholesterol and kidney function is part of good gout care. What are the symptoms of gout? Sudden, severe pain in a joint, often the big toe, usually starting at night, with redness, heat and swelling. The joint may be too painful to touch. Some people also have a fever. What uric acid level causes gout? Uric acid above 408 µmol/L (6.8 mg/dL) is high enough for crystals to form, but many people with high levels never get gout. On treatment, the target is below 360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL). What causes gout in the foot? (Punca gout di kaki) Uric acid crystals collect in the joints of the feet, especially the big toe. Risk rises with excess weight, alcohol, sugary drinks, red meat, some seafood, some medicines and kidney disease. What is the difference between gout and pseudogout? Gout is caused by uric acid crystals and often affects the big toe. Pseudogout is caused by calcium crystals, is more common over 60, and usually affects the knee. Should I stop allopurinol during a gout attack? No. Keep taking it as prescribed. Stopping and starting can trigger more attacks. Your doctor will treat the attack separately. Can gout be cured? Gout can be controlled. Keeping uric acid below the target with long-term medicine and lifestyle changes can stop attacks and dissolve tophi over time.

title: Itchy skin in Malaysia: eczema, hives (gegata) and other causes, and when to see a doctor
desc: Heat, sweat and stress make itchy skin common in Malaysia. How to tell eczema from hives (gegata), heat rash, scabies and fungal rashes, what treatment helps, and why to avoid creams with hidden steroids.
headings: What’s causing your itch? · Eczema · Beware creams with hidden steroids · Pompholyx · Hives (gegata or urticaria) · Heat rash, scabies and fungal rashes · When to see a doctor
keywords: Aesthetics & skin Itchy skin, eczema and hives Atopic dermatitis Ekzema kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Eczema causes dry, itchy, inflamed skin. Moisturising generously every day is the most important treatment. Hives (gegata, urticaria) are raised, itchy welts that move around and fade within 24 hours. Non-drowsy antihistamines usually help. Swollen lips or tongue, or difficulty breathing, with hives is an emergency. Call 999. Steroid creams are safe and effective when used as directed. Avoid “herbal” or unregistered creams, which have been found to contain hidden steroids and mercury. Itch that is worse at night and affects family members may be scabies, and ring-shaped scaly patches may be a fungal infection. Both need specific treatment. Condition What it looks like Eczema (atopic dermatitis) Dry, red or darker, rough, itchy patches, often in skin creases such as elbows, knees and neck. Comes and goes. Pompholyx Tiny, very itchy blisters on the palms, sides of the fingers and sometimes the soles Hives (gegata, urticaria) Raised, itchy welts that appear suddenly, move around, and each fade within 24 hours Heat rash (prickly heat) Tiny, prickly red spots in sweaty areas, clearing within days when cool Scabies Intense itch, worse at night, with tiny burrows between fingers, on wrists and around the waist. Often several family members. Ringworm (kurap) A ring-shaped, scaly, itchy patch that slowly spreads Pityriasis versicolor (panau) Flat, lighter or darker patches on the chest, back and upper arms, often only mildly itchy Because treatments differ, a doctor should check any rash that is spreading, not improving, or keeps coming back. Atopic eczema is common in Malaysian children. Around 1 in 8 children had symptoms in the past year in Malaysian studies, and most develop it before age 5. Many outgrow it, but it can continue into adulthood. Triggers: heat, sweating, sun, soap and detergents, rough fabrics, dust mites and stress. Malaysian guidelines found no link with humidity itself, but hot weather and sweat often make it flare. What helps: Moisturise generously , at least twice a day and after bathing, even when the skin looks clear. This is the most important treatment, and it reduces the need for steroid creams. Use a soap substitute or gentle, fragrance-free wash, and keep baths and showers short (under 10 minutes), with lukewarm water. Steroid creams prescribed by your doctor calm flares. Use the amount and strength advised. A fingertip unit (a line of cream from the tip to the first crease of an adult finger) covers an area the size of two adult palms. Used correctly, they are safe, including for children. Wear loose cotton clothes, and keep nails short to limit damage from scratching. Supplements: Malaysian guidelines found too little evidence that probiotics or vitamins B6, D or E help, and evening primrose and borage oil don’t. A doctor can confirm the cause of a rash and prescribe the right strength of treatment. Some “herbal”, “natural” or “steroid-free” eczema creams sold online contain strong steroids or mercury. In April 2026, the Ministry of Health cancelled two cosmetic products found to contain a steroid and mercury. In July 2026, Singapore’s Health Sciences Authority found a potent steroid in a “zero-steroid” herbal eczema cream bought from a Malaysian seller, after a 12-year-old gained 6 kg and developed stretch marks. Hidden steroids can thin the skin, and stopping them suddenly can cause a severe flare. Use creams from a doctor or pharmacist, check for a registration number, and if you’ve been using an unregistered cream, see a doctor before stopping it. Pompholyx (dyshidrotic eczema) causes crops of small, intensely itchy blisters on the fingers and palms, and sometimes the toes and soles. Episodes usually last 2 to 3 weeks. Triggers include heat and sweating, stress, wet hands, harsh chemicals, and nickel or cobalt. Use a moisturiser and soap substitute, keep hands dry, and don’t burst the blisters. A doctor may prescribe a short course of steroid cream, or antibiotics if the blisters become infected. Hives are raised, itchy welts that can appear anywhere. Each welt fades within 24 hours, but new ones can keep appearing. Hives lasting less than 6 weeks are called acute; longer than 6 weeks is chronic. Common causes: viral infections (especially in children), foods such as shellfish, eggs, milk and peanuts, medicines such as antibiotics, aspirin and anti-inflammatory painkillers, and insect stings. In adults, often no cause is found. Treatment: a non-drowsy antihistamine such as cetirizine or loratadine, available from pharmacies, usually controls hives. For persistent hives, a doctor may increase the dose. Avoid any trigger you identify. Call 999 if hives come with Swelling of the lips, tongue, mouth or throat Difficulty breathing or swallowing, or wheezing Pale or blue skin, confusion, dizziness or collapse These are signs of anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction. Heat rash comes from blocked sweat glands. Keep cool, wear loose cotton clothes, and avoid heavy creams. Calamine lotion can soothe it. It usually clears within a few days. Scabies is caused by tiny mites and spreads by close skin contact. It needs a prescription treatment, and everyone in the household should be treated at the same time, even without symptoms. Itching can continue for 2 to 4 weeks after successful treatment. Ringworm (kurap) is a fungal infection, treated with antifungal cream. Steroid creams can make it worse. Pityriasis versicolor (panau) is a harmless yeast overgrowth that isn’t contagious, but often comes back in hot, humid weather. Antifungal shampoos and creams help. Itch powders (bedak gatal) may feel soothing, but there is little evidence that they treat any of these conditions. Eczema that is weeping, crusted, painful or spreading fast , or comes with fever. These are signs of infection. Hives that last more than a couple of days, keep coming back, or come with swelling under the skin A rash that isn’t improving with simple care, or you aren’t sure what it is Itch that keeps you or your child awake Any rash in a baby that worries you What is gegata? Gegata is a common Malay term for hives (urticaria): raised, itchy welts that appear suddenly and fade within 24 hours. Non-drowsy antihistamines usually help. Swelling of the lips or difficulty breathing is an emergency. What are the symptoms of eczema? Dry, itchy, inflamed skin, often in creases such as the elbows, knees and neck. It can look red on lighter skin and darker brown or grey on darker skin, and comes and goes in flares. What is pompholyx eczema? A type of eczema that causes small, very itchy blisters on the palms and fingers, sometimes the soles. It is often triggered by heat, sweat, stress or contact with metals and chemicals. Are steroid creams safe for eczema? Yes, when used as your doctor directs, at the right strength and amount. Problems usually come from overuse, or from unregistered creams with hidden strong steroids. Do supplements help eczema? Malaysian guidelines found too little evidence for probiotics and vitamins, and evening primrose oil doesn’t help. Daily moisturising remains the most effective step. How do I know if my itch is scabies? Scabies itch is usually worse at night, with tiny lines or spots between the fingers, on the wrists or around the waist, and often several family members itch. See a doctor, as the whole household needs treatment.

title: Floods and your health: leptospirosis, diarrhoea and other risks during the monsoon
desc: The Northeast Monsoon has begun, and floods have already hit Penang and Kedah. The illnesses floods bring, the leptospirosis symptoms to watch for, and how to stay safe during and after a flood.
headings: The monsoon season has begun · Illnesses to watch for during and after floods · Leptospirosis: the flood fever to know about · Melioidosis: a risk for people with diabetes · Safe water and food · Cuts, wounds and tetanus · Cleaning up safely · Dengue after the floods · Looking after your mind · Useful contacts
keywords: Prevention Floods and your health Leptospirosis Leptospirosis (kencing tikus) denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: The Northeast Monsoon runs from 27 October 2026 to March 2027, with 3 to 5 episodes of heavy rain expected between November and January. Most illnesses in flood relief centres are chest and skin infections, but floodwater can also spread diarrhoea, hepatitis A and leptospirosis. Leptospirosis (kencing tikus) can start 2 to 30 days after contact with floodwater. See a doctor for fever, headache, muscle aches or red eyes, and mention the flood. Drink boiled or bottled water, throw away food that touched floodwater, and cover cuts with waterproof plasters. Never run a generator indoors, never mix bleach with other cleaners, and clear standing water after the flood to stop dengue mosquitoes breeding. MetMalaysia says the 2026/27 Northeast Monsoon began on 27 October 2026 and will last until March 2027. It expects 3 to 5 episodes of continuous heavy rain between November and January, followed by drier weather from January. Floods have already started. On 25 October, heavy rain caused flash floods at 10 locations on Penang island, and a 73-year-old resident died in a landslide in Paya Terubong. In Kedah, 202 people from 69 families were in relief centres in Yan on 27 October, and the state has listed 90 flood hotspots. On 28 October, five relief centres were open nationwide, in Kedah and Selangor. Check river levels on the Department of Irrigation and Drainage’s Public Infobanjir site, and follow MetMalaysia’s weather warnings. The Ministry of Health and the National Security Council list these as the main flood-related diseases: Diarrhoea and food poisoning , including dysentery and, rarely, cholera Hepatitis A and E , from contaminated water and food Leptospirosis , from water or mud contaminated with animal urine Chest infections and flu, which spread easily in crowded relief centres Skin infections and eye infections (conjunctivitis) Dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases, after the water recedes In practice, most people who fall ill in relief centres have chest and skin infections. During the November 2025 floods, health teams treated 2,083 people in relief centres. The most common problems were respiratory infections (376 cases) and skin infections (92), with 15 cases of gastroenteritis. In the larger November–December 2024 floods, there were 6,730 respiratory infections, 3,021 skin infections and 298 cases of gastroenteritis. No outbreaks were declared in either year. Leptospirosis, often called kencing tikus (rat urine disease), is caused by bacteria in the urine of rats and other animals. The bacteria survive for weeks in water and wet soil, and enter the body through cuts, scratches, the eyes, nose or mouth. Wading or cleaning up in floodwater is a common way to catch it. It has been a notifiable disease in Malaysia since 2010. Symptoms usually start 5 to 14 days after exposure, but can appear anywhere from 2 to 30 days: Sudden fever, chills and headache Muscle aches Red eyes Vomiting, diarrhoea, or a rash Most cases are mild, but some people develop a severe form with yellow skin and eyes (jaundice), kidney failure or bleeding in the lungs, which can be fatal. See a doctor early If you get a fever within a month of contact with floodwater or mud, see a doctor and tell them about the flood . Leptospirosis is treated with antibiotics, which work best when started early. It can look like dengue or flu at first. If you are going into floodwater for rescue or clean-up work, ask your doctor whether preventive antibiotics are suitable for you. Melioidosis is a less well-known infection caused by bacteria that live in soil and muddy water. Cases rise after heavy rain and floods. It mostly affects people with diabetes , kidney or liver disease, or thalassaemia. In one Pahang study, about three-quarters of patients had diabetes. Symptoms, which can start 1 to 3 weeks after exposure, include fever, cough, chest pain or abscesses. It needs weeks of hospital antibiotics, so see a doctor early for any fever after a flood if you have diabetes. Drink boiled or bottled water until the authorities say tap water is safe. Bring water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. If it is cloudy, let it settle and filter it through a clean cloth first. Throw away any food that touched floodwater, including packaged food that isn’t in a sealed can, and food from a fridge that lost power for a long time. Don’t wash food, dishes or yourself in floodwater. Wash your hands with soap and clean water before eating and after cleaning up. For diarrhoea, drink oral rehydration salts (ORS) and plenty of clean fluids. See a doctor for blood in the stool, high fever, or signs of dehydration, especially in children and older people. Wear boots and gloves in floodwater and mud, and avoid wading where you can. Cover cuts with waterproof plasters before going into water. If you get a cut, wash it well with clean water and soap, and keep it clean and dry. Flood wounds count as dirty wounds. See a doctor for a tetanus booster if your last one was 5 or more years ago, or if you aren’t sure. See a doctor if a wound becomes red, swollen, hot or painful, or leaks pus. Turn off electricity at the main switch before entering a flooded home if you can do so safely, and have wet electrical items checked before use. Never run a generator indoors , in a garage or near windows. Keep it at least 6 metres from doors, windows and vents. Generators produce carbon monoxide, which can kill without warning. Protect yourself with boots, gloves, goggles and, if there is mould, an N95 mask. Open windows while you clean. Remove mud first , then wash hard surfaces with soap and water and disinfect them with diluted bleach: no more than 1 cup (about 240 ml) of household bleach in about 4.5 litres of water. Never mix bleach with ammonia or other cleaners. It makes a toxic gas. Throw away soaked mattresses, carpets and soft items that can’t be dried within 24 to 48 hours, as mould grows quickly. As floodwater recedes, it leaves puddles, blocked drains and water-filled containers where Aedes mosquitoes breed. Dengue cases in Malaysia have already passed 78,000 this year. After a flood, walk around your home and empty anything holding water, and use mosquito repellent. See our guide to dengue warning signs . Clear standing water after a flood to stop Aedes mosquitoes breeding. Losing belongings, being displaced or worrying about the next flood is stressful. Trouble sleeping, irritability and anxiety are common afterwards, and children may become clingy or upset. Talk to someone you trust, keep to routines where you can, and ask for help if it doesn’t ease. The Ministry of Health’s Talian HEAL 15555 offers free psychosocial support. Need Where to go Emergency, rescue or ambulance Call 999 (112 from a mobile) River and flood levels Public Infobanjir (Department of Irrigation and Drainage) Open relief centres (PPS) InfoBencana (Department of Social Welfare) Weather warnings MetMalaysia, hotline 1-300-22-1638 Emotional support Talian HEAL 15555 What diseases can you get from floodwater? The main risks are diarrhoea and food poisoning, hepatitis A, leptospirosis, skin and eye infections, and chest infections in crowded relief centres. Dengue can rise after the water recedes. What are the symptoms of leptospirosis (kencing tikus)? Sudden fever, headache, chills, muscle aches and red eyes, sometimes with vomiting, diarrhoea or a rash. Symptoms usually start 5 to 14 days after contact with contaminated water, but can take up to 30 days. Is leptospirosis curable? Yes. It is treated with antibiotics, which work best when started early. See a doctor for any fever after contact with floodwater, and tell them about the flood. Is it safe to drink tap water after a flood? Not until the authorities say so. Drink bottled water, or bring tap water to a rolling boil for 1 minute before drinking or cooking with it. Do I need a tetanus jab after a flood injury? If you get a cut or puncture wound in floodwater and your last tetanus booster was 5 or more years ago, or you aren’t sure, see a doctor about a booster. When does the 2026 monsoon season end? MetMalaysia expects the Northeast Monsoon to last from 27 October 2026 to March 2027, with the heaviest rain between November and January.

title: HFMD in children: symptoms, how long it’s contagious, home care and warning signs
desc: Hand, foot and mouth disease spreads fast in taska and tadika. The symptoms in babies and children, how long it stays contagious, how to ease mouth ulcers, the warning signs that need hospital care, and how it differs from measles.
headings: HFMD in Malaysia · HFMD symptoms in babies and children · How long is HFMD contagious? · Caring for a child with HFMD at home · Warning signs that need urgent care · Preventing HFMD · HFMD or measles?
keywords: Prevention HFMD in children Hand, foot and mouth disease Penyakit tangan, kaki dan mulut denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: HFMD usually starts with fever, sore throat and poor appetite, followed by painful mouth ulcers and spots or blisters on the hands, feet and bottom. It is caused by several viruses, mainly coxsackieviruses and enteroviruses. Most children recover in 7 to 10 days. It is most contagious in the first week, but the virus can stay in stools for weeks. Handwashing is the best protection. The main risk is dehydration from painful mouth ulcers. Offer cool drinks and soft food, and give paracetamol for pain. Seek urgent care for drowsiness, jerking during sleep, weakness, persistent vomiting, breathing difficulty or passing very little urine. HFMD has been a notifiable disease in Malaysia since 2007, and cases rise and fall from year to year. 2025 was a very large year: Malaysia recorded 239,907 cases by late August, and more than 1,100 childcare centres and kindergartens were ordered to close in the first months of the year to stop the spread. 2026 has been much quieter. The Ministry of Health reported 40,879 cases as of 22 August 2026 , about 83% fewer than in the same period of 2025. Most infections this year were caused by coxsackievirus A6 and other enteroviruses. Enterovirus 71 (EV71), the type more often linked to serious complications, made up only 1.5% of enteroviruses detected. When there is an outbreak, health officers can order a nursery or kindergarten to close for 10 days, roughly two incubation periods, under the Prevention and Control of Infectious Diseases Act 1988. Symptoms usually start 3 to 5 days after a child catches the virus: First 1 to 2 days: fever, sore throat, tiredness and not wanting to eat or drink. Then: painful mouth ulcers on the tongue, gums and inside the cheeks, and a spotty rash on the palms and soles, sometimes on the bottom, legs or arms. The spots can turn into small blisters. The rash is usually not itchy . In babies and toddlers , you may notice irritability, drooling, refusing feeds or the bottle because the mouth hurts, and fewer wet nappies. Not every child gets all the symptoms. Some have only mouth ulcers or only a rash. Very rarely, a child’s fingernails or toenails may peel or fall off a few weeks later. They grow back normally. Most children with HFMD recover at home within 7 to 10 days. A child can spread HFMD a few days before symptoms appear. They are most contagious in the first week of illness. The virus can stay in saliva for days and in stools for weeks after the child feels better, and people without symptoms can spread it too. It spreads through saliva, coughs and sneezes, fluid from blisters, and stools, for example during nappy changes, or from shared toys and cups. When can my child go back to taska or school? The Ministry of Health advises keeping children with symptoms at home and away from childcare centres and public places. Overseas guidance suggests returning once the child feels well and has no fever or uncontrolled drooling. Many nurseries have their own rules and may ask for a doctor’s letter, so check with them. Children and adults can catch HFMD more than once , because several different viruses cause it. There is no specific medicine for HFMD, and antibiotics don’t work against it. Care focuses on comfort and fluids: Keep them drinking. Dehydration is the main risk. Offer small sips often: cool water, milk, or oral rehydration salts. Ice chips or cold drinks can soothe mouth ulcers. Avoid acidic drinks such as orange juice, which sting. Soft, cool foods such as yoghurt, porridge, soup and soft rice. Avoid hot, salty and spicy food. Paracetamol for fever and mouth pain, dosed by your child’s weight. A pharmacist can suggest a mouth gel suitable for your child’s age. Never give aspirin to children. Skin: the rash usually needs no treatment. Keep blisters clean and dry, and let them dry up on their own. Calamine lotion isn’t usually needed. If a spot is itchy, use it only on unbroken skin, never in the mouth or on burst blisters, and ask a doctor first for children under 2. Avoid ibuprofen if your child is dehydrated or if dengue is possible. See our guide to fever medicine for children . Serious complications are rare, but some viruses, especially EV71, can affect the brain or heart. Children under 5, and especially under 2, are at highest risk. Go to a hospital emergency department or call 999 if your child has Unusual drowsiness, or is hard to wake or very irritable Sudden jerking or twitching, especially during sleep Weakness, unsteadiness or difficulty walking Persistent vomiting, or a high fever that won’t come down with medicine Fast or difficult breathing Signs of dehydration: passing very little urine, a dry mouth, no tears, or very few wet nappies A seizure See a GP sooner if your child is under 6 months old, has a weak immune system, or isn’t improving after 7 to 10 days. Wash hands with soap and water, especially after nappy changes and using the toilet, and before eating. Teach children to do the same. Clean toys, toilets and surfaces regularly with soap or a household disinfectant. Don’t share cups, cutlery, towels or toothbrushes. Keep sick children at home until they are well. Is there an HFMD vaccine? Not in Malaysia. Vaccines against EV71 are used in China, and an application to bring one to Malaysia for children aged 6 months to 6 years is under review by the NPRA. These vaccines protect only against EV71, not the other viruses that cause most HFMD. Searches for measles have been rising alongside HFMD. Measles is far more serious, and both cause fever and a rash, so it helps to know the difference: HFMD Measles Early symptoms Fever, sore throat, poor appetite High fever, cough, runny nose, red watery eyes Mouth Painful ulcers Tiny white spots inside the cheeks (Koplik spots) Rash Spots or blisters mainly on palms, soles and bottom Red, blotchy rash starting at the hairline and spreading down the whole body Vaccine None in Malaysia MMR, free under the National Immunisation Programme Malaysia recorded 3,791 measles cases in 2024 , up from 2,002 in 2023, and 3 children died, all unvaccinated. The National Immunisation Programme gives the MMR vaccine at 9 and 12 months , with an extra early dose in Sabah. If your child has missed a measles vaccine, ask at your Klinik Kesihatan about a free catch-up dose. See our vaccination schedule guide . If you think your child has measles, call the clinic before you go, so staff can keep other patients safe. What are the symptoms of HFMD in children? (Simptom HFMD kanak-kanak) Fever, sore throat and poor appetite, followed by painful mouth ulcers and a spotty rash or small blisters on the palms, soles and sometimes the bottom. Symptoms start 3 to 5 days after infection. What are the signs of HFMD in a baby? Babies may be irritable, drool more, refuse feeds because of mouth ulcers, have a fever, and have spots on the hands, feet or nappy area. Watch for fewer wet nappies, a sign of dehydration. How long is HFMD contagious? A child is most contagious in the first week of illness, but can spread the virus a few days before symptoms appear, and the virus can stay in stools for weeks. Good handwashing is essential. Is calamine lotion good for HFMD? It isn’t usually needed, as the HFMD rash is rarely itchy.
